first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and the archived evidence indicates that reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding improved early adoption. A small guarded test is the best fit for the single weekly slot and can measure completion, activation, time-to-value, and qualified downstream revenue while limiting the risk of attracting low-intent accounts. Promotional pricing may address competitor pressure, but its downstream revenue quality and sustainability should remain uncertain without verification.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, instrumented onboarding-simplification experiment focused on SMB and self-serve accounts. The evidence directly addresses both current problems: signup simplification lifted activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%, while shortened onboarding improved completion 13%, time-to-value by 2.1 days, and retention 3%. Monitor qualified revenue and 30-day retention as guardrails because signup simplification previously reduced retention 1% and has not been validated beyond SMB. Do not broadly roll out until downstream revenue quality and retention remain positive.

final2.rationale: Respond to the competitor's deeper SMB price cut with a targeted, time-limited promotional pricing test for price-sensitive SMB prospects and at-risk accounts. Prior memory indicates strong acquisition and revenue lift for this segment, but the source cannot be reverified this cycle. Protect sustainable qualified revenue with eligibility limits, expiration dates, margin thresholds, retention monitoring, and comparison against a holdout; do not broadly reduce list pricing.
